content.text: {"relation": "DIVERGENT", "consensus_summary": "Righteousness is primarily right standing before God — a status graciously credited (imputed) to believers through faith in Christ apart from works — together with the ethical conformity to God's character that flows from that status. Symbolized by a bestowed garment/robe (Isa 61:10; Rev 19:8), grounded in Gen 15:6, Rom 1:17, 3:21-26, 4:3-8, 2 Cor 5:21, Phil 3:9. Alternatives include infused/transformative righteousness, ethical conduct, covenant faithfulness, social justice, and Christ himself as righteousness.", "book_summary": "Righteousness is the doing of God's commandments — the law actually kept, worn as the garment of righteous acts. The book explicitly rejects both 'a vague goodness' and 'a verdict only received,' i.e., it denies the imputed-status reading it labels as the common teaching, citing Deut 6:25, Ps 119:172, and 1 John 3:7.", "consensus_core_identification": "Righteousness = a right standing before God received by faith apart from works (forensic/imputed status), which then produces upright conduct.", "book_core_identification": "Righteousness = the performed keeping of God's commandments (righteous deeds themselves), expressly not a received verdict or credited status.", "core_relation": "CONTRADICTS", "extension_relation": "BOOK_SUBSET", "boundary_disagreement": "The book retains only the conduct-side of the consensus extension (righteous acts, obedience, the 'garment of righteous acts' as in Rev 19:8) and excludes the entire status-side: believers counted righteous by faith apart from works (Gen 15:6; Rom 4:3-8) are, on the book's definition, not thereby righteous unless they do the commandments. What the consensus treats as the dominant referent, the book reclassifies as a misidentification.", "material_contradiction": "The consensus's dominant identification says righteousness is 'counted apart from works' (Rom 4:3-8) and 'not my own... but through faith' (Phil 3:9); the book says righteousness IS the works — 'it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments' (Deut 6:25) — and explicitly negates 'a verdict only received.' Both cannot be the primary sense of the same term in the same salvific context: a status received apart from doing cannot be identical to the doing itself once the book denies the status reading.", "rationale": "The book's positive content (righteousness as ethical obedience) appears in the consensus as a listed 'common' alternative, so this is not NOVEL. But the entry does more than narrow: its explicit denial clause ('not... a verdict only received') and its common-view note show it is rejecting and replacing the consensus's central identification (imputed right standing by faith), not merely tightening its boundary. Accepting the book's definition requires rejecting the imputed-forensic core that all three blind responses put at the center. This is core contradiction with a subset extension — the book keeps the deeds cases while expelling the status cases — which the rubric classifies as DIVERGENT rather than REFINED.", "citation_support": "PARTIAL", "strongest_objection": "The strongest objection to DIVERGENT is that the consensus core is explicitly dual — 'legal/relational status AND ethical quality' — and the book merely elevates the ethical member (already listed as a 'common' alternative with 1 John 3:7 as a proof text) while demoting the forensic member, which would make this a REFINED narrowing within the consensus's own range rather than a replacement. Against this, the book's own framing treats the imputed-status view as the erroneous common teaching to be corrected, which is contradiction, not boundary adjustment.", "confidence": "high"}
